The 1st accused Zung Kyung-san claims in his
statement that he resigned of his own accord from the post
of camp manager because of his intention to leave Shanghai,
but investigations made at the Federation of Charity
Organizations, reveal that this statement is not true.
According to Mr. Chao Poh-ch'u, Chief of the Refugee
Reception Section of the Federation, the Federation received
on October 22 an annonymous letter stating that the 1st
accused, the then Manager of the Dee Loong Camp, was
embezzling the rice issued to the camp and an investigation
was commenced in which the allegation was more or less
confirmed, but sufficient evidence was not forthcoming, so
Mr. Chao Poh-ch'u on October 24 asked the 1st accused to
resign his position in the camp.

It will be seen in the statement of the 1st accused
that he denied having the intention of retaining those four
girl students and of sending them to the interior but in the
statement of the 4th accused Li Chun it will be seen that
on November 17 he and the 1st accused instructed the girls
to be present at the Yuan Tan Lodging House at noon November
18, should they want to leave Shanghai, which the four girls
did. The four girl victims also stated that the 1st accused
Zung informed them that $100 would be required for travelling
expenses if they decided to go with the group. Further he
knew the parents of those girls and even visited one of them
on November 18th but made no mention that their daughter was
about to leave Shanghai even when he knew the parents objected.

My name is Yang Yang alias Yang Ngoeh-hwa (real name). I am 19 years old, a native of Peiping and single. I reside at Room 7, 150 Bank of China Employees' Quarters, Jessfield Road, O.C.L. I am a student of the Jao Kwang Middle School, corner of Haiphong and Ferry Roads. I was engaged to marry Zung Kyung-san (陳金三) alias Sung Koo-jen (沈可人) (1st accused) in January, 1938. My father is an employee of the Registry of the General Affairs Department of the Bank of China, Hongkong.

During the summer vacation of 1937, I was a member of the Students' Circles National Salvation Association, Pootung Guild Building, 1545 Avenue Edward VII. I meanwhile joined the "Service Group to Villages" (農村服務團) formed by Mr. Pan Kung-chan (潘公展), Commissioner of the now defunct Bureau of Social Affairs, Shanghai City Government, and proceeded to Wusieh, where I, together with 90 others, carried out propaganda work among the farmers for the promotion of public health, opium suppression and national salvation.

About two months ago, my fiance and I promoted the 6th War Service Party of the Shanghai Students' Wandering Group (上海學生流亡團) with a communication address in the Dee Loong Refugee Camp (棣隆), North Shanse Road. The object of this group is to recruit local students and ex-students willing to proceed to the interior and to send them inland. I know that this group is supported by Mr. Wong Chao-dz (王造時).

My name is Yang/Shing-ts. I am 40 years of

My name is Li Chun ( 李 群 ), alias Zia

Canton and single. I reside at 25 Yung An Fang, Rue

Fuhtan Middle School, Avenue Haig.

Following the outbreak of hostilities, 1937, I
became a member of the now defunct Choral Circles National
Salvation Association, Ming Kwang Middle School on Kiaochow
Road. During the summer vacation of 1938, I joined the
Chinese Y.M.C.A., 123 Boulevard de Montigny, which assigned
me to teach refugee children in a refugee camp on Rue Hue.

Livelihood" and "Emancipation" from my school mates. I

SHANGHAI, 30th. November 1938.

T. Robertson Esq.
Deputy Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

According to report my brother Yao Zung (姚拯) is now
being detained in the Sinza Police Station. Being his elder
brother and guardian, I make bold to ask your kindness to permit
him to be released on bail.

Because he disappeared, our grand-mother worried so much
that she fell very sick, and has been anxious to see the grand-
son. His release will mostly probably make the old lady better
and recover sooner.

I have been a member of the Special Police for seven years
and I have a very good record. My brother's detention is a
stain on my reputation. Hoping that my humble request will
receive your favourable consideration.

Your faithfully.
N. S. Yao

From enquiries made, it was learned that the four
girls, (1) Zung Wei Lai, (2) Wong Pei Nyoh, (3) Nyue
Mai Ling & (4) Zung Kwei Ying, were all student friends
attending the Shanghai Middle School, 466 Chengtu Road,
and about one week ago they planned to run away from
home and proceed to Wenchow to take part in Red Cross
work. About 2p.m. on 15-11-38 they went to the Zung Kyi
Daung (仁濟堂) Welfare Association, Yunnan Road, and
requested free passages to Wenchow, but this was refused,
and they were advised to return to their homes. On
leaving the above institution, they stood discussing the
matter, when the 4th accused approached them and informed
them that he knew someone who could get them free.

(3) 杨胡氏（Yang Woo Sz），40岁，北平人，家庭妇女，住址杰斯菲尔德路宗安坊（Tsoong Ang Ph S）37号。

第一、第二及第三名被告由法国警察移交，并于1938年11月19日凌晨1时30分，根据从第一名被告处获得的情报，在北山西路568弄3号的一个难民收容所内逮捕了另一名中国男子：
(4) 李群（Lee Kyuin），15岁，广东人，无业，住址同上。

经查询获悉，这四名女孩，(1) 张美兰（Zung Wei Lai，译注：此处原文拼写与上文 Tang Wei Lai 不一致，依原文译），(2) 王佩玉（Wong Pei Nyoh，译注：此处拼写与上文 Wong Pei Hyoh 略有不同），(3) 李美龄（Nyue Mai Ling，译注：此处拼写与上文 Nyue Hai Ling 略有不同）及 (4) 张桂英（Zung Kwei Ying，译注：此处原文拼写与上文 Tang Kwei Ying 不一致，依原文译），均为就读于成都路466号上海中学的同学好友。约一周前，她们计划离家出走，前往温州参加红十字会工作。1938年11月15日下午2时许，她们前往云南路的仁济堂（Zung Kyi Daung）福利协会，申请免费前往温州的路费，但遭到拒绝，并被劝回家。离开上述机构后，她们站在那里讨论此事，此时第四名被告走近她们，告知她们他认识可以帮她们搞到免费路费的人。

1938年11月18日下午1时许，四名女孩自行前往上述寄宿房屋的28号房间，在那里见到了第一和第二名被告，随后第三和第四名被告也加入其中。第一名被告告诉女孩们，需要大约100元作为旅费，于是王佩玉和李美龄两名女孩前往成都路上海中学，试图筹集一些钱并取回个人物品。她们被学校职员扣留，并通知了她们的父母，结果导致本警署接到如上所述的报案。

Recovery of 7 male Chinese alleged
to have been abducted from Frenchtown.
--------------------------------------------------
At 8.37.p.m. on 17.4.1940 a teleprinter
message (T.B.C.13) was received from the French Police
requesting information regarding 8 youths ages from
14 to 17 who it was believed were intending to leave
Shanghai without the consent of their parents.

At 12.40.a.m. on 18.4.1940 C.P.Cs 472 & 346
telephoned to station to the effect that having know-
ledge of this enquiry they had made enquiries in the
lodging houses on their beat and had located seven
likely persons in the Woo Hyung (汪屋寓) Lodging house,
239 Cunningham Road. Enquiries were made by D.S.I.
Guess and C.D.C.276 and the seven youths were brought

April 18, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao :-

MISSING STUDENTS OF LOCAL MIDDLE SCHOOLS BECOME CAPTIVES
OF JAPANESE IN NANKING AND SOOCHOW

Of late the French Municipal Police have been repeatedly receiving reports from the residents of the French Concession informing them that more than ten students of the various middle schools in the French Concession have gone missing. The close search made by the French Police of the various hotels and apartments in the Concession in the past ten days in the hope of obtaining clues of the missing students has proved a failure.

Yesterday about 6 of the missing students suddenly returned to their homes. They were immediately called upon by the French Police for inquiries, as a result of which it was found that they were patriotic youths who desired to proceed to the fallen areas south of the Yangtze to join the Chinese New 4th Route Army and the rest of the Chinese National Army at Chinghua, Ningpo, or to enlist in the Military College of the National Government in Chungking. However, they failed to complete their trip because of lack of passage money. Also a shameless traitor who pretended to be a member of the New 4th Route National Army and of the National Government in Chungking, played a trick on the students by telling them that he would be responsible for sending them to their destinations. All these young students, not having had much experience, fell into the trap. They were sent by ship to Nanking and other fallen areas and also some of them were taken to Soochow overland. It is learned that upon their arrival at the various places, they were forced to become soldiers.

The 6 students who safely returned to Shanghai yesterday were lucky enough to make their escape from the hands of their abductor.

As a matter of public safety and good order in the French Concession, the French Police is paying strict attention to this serious affair. It has issued an order to arrest all kidnappers of students in order to bring them to book for their crimes.

（批：Gee C 18/4 W. Kung-hua report. 19/4/40）

1940年4月18日。
晨间翻译。

《大美晚报》：

本地中学生失踪，在南京和苏州沦为日本人俘虏

近来，法租界公董局警察多次接到法租界居民报告，称法租界各中学的十多名学生失踪。过去十天里，法国警察对租界内的各家旅馆和公寓进行了严密搜查，希望能获得失踪学生的线索，但均未成功。

昨天，约6名失踪学生突然回到家中。法国警察立即传唤他们进行询问，结果发现他们是爱国青年，希望前往长江以南的沦陷区，加入在金华、宁波的中国新四军和中国国民革命军其余部队，或考入重庆国民政府的军校。然而，由于缺乏路费，他们未能完成行程。此外，一个无耻的汉奸冒充新四军和重庆国民政府成员，欺骗学生，声称负责将他们送往目的地。所有这些年轻学生因缺乏经验，落入陷阱。他们被用船运送到南京和其他沦陷区，其中一些人还通过陆路被带到苏州。据悉，到达各地后，他们被迫当兵。

昨天安全返回上海的6名学生幸运地从绑匪手中逃脱。

为了法租界的公共安全和良好秩序，法国警察正密切关注这一严重事件。已发布命令逮捕所有绑架学生的罪犯，以便将其绳之以法。

（批：Gee C 4月18日 W. Kung-hua 报告。1940年4月19日）
